extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships (postdoctoral researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/application rules for candidates applying to EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships, including mobility, publication, application-system, and reapplication policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD completion requirement for awardees
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are still pursuing your PhD you can apply, but if awarded you must provide your PhD degree before the starting date of your fellowship. You must also start your fellowship within 9 months of the offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who have not yet been awarded their PhD may apply, but the degree must be provided prior to fellowship start; fellowship must commence within 9 months of offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-year post-PhD eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: You are eligible only if you submit your application within two years after the date of award of your PhD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: if PhD awarded 1 Jan 2021, application must be fully submitted by 1 Jan 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for career breaks affecting the 2-year limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions may be granted for applicants with official career breaks that have affected their capability to apply during the relevant 2-year eligibility period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifying breaks include parental leave, mandatory military service, severe illness and other extraordinary personal circumstances. The Fellowships Office must be contacted prior to submitting a claim for an exception; applications submitted without prior approval of an exception will be deemed ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD holders eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with an MD may apply if they have appropriate research experience comparable to a PhD and meet all other eligibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, send an updated CV and a summary proposal (including intended biological insight) to the Fellowships Office. CV should list positions, research papers and previous funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of PhD award date variability
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of PhD award may be interpreted differently across doctoral education systems (defense date, programme completion date, diploma date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check directly with the institution where they obtained their degree to determine the relevant date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement: first/joint-first author paper
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have at least one first (or joint first) author primary research paper accepted for publication or published in an international peer reviewed journal or a refereed preprint at the time the application is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers submitted or under review will not be considered. EMBO recognises refereed preprints as an eligibility criterion (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research scope must align with EMBO subject areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed projects must fall within EMBO’s scientific scope/subject areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure, check the EMBO subject areas page; if still in doubt, contact the Fellowships Office with an updated CV and a short summary proposal that includes the biological question and intended biological insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for pursuing fellowship in non-EMBC Member States
rubrics_metrics.description: To pursue a fellowship in a non-EMBC Member State (e.g., US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand), you must meet all 3 conditions: 1) be national of an EMBC Member State; 2) have completed your PhD in an EMBC Member State; 3) be moving from an EMBC Member State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of EMBC Member States is provided; all three conditions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to pursue fellowship in an EMBC Member State
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply to pursue your fellowship in an EMBC Member State regardless of your nationality or the country where you obtained your PhD, provided that there is a change of country and you meet all other eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The key requirement is a change of country for the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility to work in same country as PhD studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to work in a country where the applicant developed their PhD studies are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits applying to remain in the same country where the PhD was undertaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on current presence at host institute/country
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are already at your host institute/country you can apply only if you haven’t been in the institute/country for more than 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: started at institute 1 June 2022 → must submit by 1 Dec 2022. If you have been in host country for more than 6 months but for non-research purposes, contact the Fellowships Office to determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior short research visits to host country allowed only if <6 months total
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously conducted research visits to the country where you intend to undertake the fellowship are allowed only if your stay there was of less than 6 months, either in one or several visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cumulative time across visits is considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application system: text-only, no attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: The online application system supports text only (no figures or graphs) and does not accept attached documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send reference letters or other documents to the Fellowship Office as these cannot be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee and host supervisor forms must be completed online
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees and the host supervisor should complete their recommendations via the online form; the system will not allow submission without completed reference forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure referees receive and complete the link; ask them to check spam folders if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing referee/host information after activation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you made a mistake when filling out referee/host supervisor information and have already activated the contact, the Fellowship Office can re-set the referee/host supervisor form so you can insert new/corrected information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email the Fellowships Office explaining which referee (name) and your own name so they can find your application in the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if referee did not receive recommendation link
rubrics_metrics.description: If a referee did not receive the link to provide the recommendation, contact the Fellowships Office with the referee's name and the email address you registered so the Office can assist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also advise referees to check spam folders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unable to change application after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to make changes to the application after it has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check all information before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: If PhD supervisor cannot provide a reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If your PhD supervisor cannot provide a reference, contact the Fellowship Office as soon as possible explaining why; the Office will consider requests on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early contact is required for case-by-case consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success rate and volume information
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO receives on average 600 applications per evaluation round; the success rate is around 15%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is informational for applicants about competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: No individual feedback for rejected applications
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO cannot provide individual feedback and does not have comments from the fellowship committee for rejected applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect personalized reviewer comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication policy and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reapplication is allowed only once (you can apply only two times in total) provided you meet eligibility each time. Significant changes must be applied when reapplying and clearly listed in the corresponding section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that are a mere copy of the first application will not be considered and will be immediately rejected. A submission is counted as an application once receipt is acknowledged and a reference number assigned. Previous applications cannot be automatically re-considered for new rounds; applicants must follow the same procedure and re-apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official host lab/supervisor limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: As an EMBO fellow you can only have one official host lab and one official host supervisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may propose collaboration with other labs, but must choose one main supervisor and one main lab and describe planned collaborations in the research proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior collaboration with intended host lowers priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to work with host laboratories with which the candidate has collaborated in the past generally receive lower priority for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt about eligibility or priority, contact the Fellowships Office with an updated CV and summary proposal emphasizing intended biological insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institute director information is a formality
rubrics_metrics.description: Information related to the receiving institute’s director is requested as a formality because, if awarded, the director might need to sign the grant agreement between the host institution and EMBO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not required from the director during the application process; another authority/representative can sign if the director is not available.
